close_reason: Self-parent guard added at filenode.rs:489+ with new regression test set_update_self_parent_returns_invalid_properties. Fix is cheap (id equality before backend call) and the test seeds no descendants so the guard, not the existing descendant-set check, is what the assertion exercises. Committed in 225603e. Gates: fmt/clippy/test/doc all green.
description:
draft-ietf-jmap-filenode-13 §3.2.3 (lines 527-529): 'an attempt to move a node to a parent for which this node is also an ancestor is an error, and an invalidProperties error will be returned'. A node is trivially an ancestor of itself, so setting parentId = id is the simplest cycle.

The current src/filenode.rs:489-515 calls get_descendant_ids(id) and checks whether the proposed new_parent_id appears in the descendant set. Per the FileNodeBackend trait doc (src/backend.rs:85-90 and PLAN.md): 'The return value includes the ids of all descendants at all depths, but NOT the id of the node itself.' Therefore the case new_parent_id == id is never caught by descendant_ids.iter().any(|did| did == &new_parent_id).

Trigger: client sends FileNode/set update { 'node1': { 'parentId': 'node1' } }. Bad behavior: handler passes the patch to backend.update_object, which (depending on backend) either accepts the self-parent (data corruption: tree no longer well-founded) or rejects it for unrelated reasons.

Required fix: explicit guard 'if new_parent_id == id { return invalidProperties }' before or alongside the descendant set check at src/filenode.rs:494.
title: Cycle check misses self-parent (setting parentId = id)
